recipes.name: Oats Upma with Mixed Vegetables and Paneer
recipes.health_benefit: Rich in soluble fiber from oats, which can help lower LDL cholesterol. Vegetables provide essential vitamins and antioxidants, while paneer adds lean protein.

ingredients.item: Mixed vegetables (carrots, peas, beans, bell peppers)

instructions: Dry roast oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until lightly fragrant. Set aside.
Heat mustard oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves, green chili, and grated ginger.
Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent.
Add chopped mixed vegetables and turmeric powder. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender.
Add 1.5 cups of water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, add roasted oats gradually, stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Cover and cook for 3-5 minutes until oats absorb water.
Stir in low-fat paneer cubes. Remove from heat, stir in lemon juice and garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Grilled Surmai (Kingfish) with Steamed Broccoli
recipes.health_benefit: Excellent source of Omega-3 fatty acids, which help lower triglycerides and may modestly lower LDL. Surmai is also a good source of Vitamin D. Broccoli provides fiber and antioxidants.
instructions: Marinate the surmai fillet with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, red chili, coriander, cumin powder, salt, and juice from half a lemon. Let it sit for 15-20 minutes.
Preheat grill pan or oven to medium-high.
Lightly brush the marinated fish with mustard oil. Grill for 4-5 minutes on each side, or until cooked through and flaky.
Meanwhile, steam broccoli florets for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Serve grilled fish with steamed broccoli and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Multigrain Roti with Dal Palak and Bhindi Sabzi
recipes.health_benefit: Multigrain roti and dal palak provide excellent soluble fiber for LDL cholesterol management. Lentils are a good source of lean protein, and spinach adds iron and other vitamins. Bhindi (okra) also contributes soluble fiber.

ingredients.quantity: 2 tsp (1 tsp for dal, 1 tsp for sabzi)

instructions: For Dal Palak: Wash masoor dal and cook in a pressure cooker with 1.5 cups water, a pinch of turmeric, and salt until tender (2-3 whistles). Heat 1 tsp mustard oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, chopped onion, green chili, ginger-garlic paste. Sauté until golden. Add chopped tomato, turmeric, red chili, coriander powder. Cook until oil separates. Add chopped spinach and cook until wilted. Add the cooked dal, a little water if needed, and garam masala. Simmer for 5 minutes. Garnish with coriander.

For Bhindi Sabzi: Wash and pat dry bhindi, then chop. Heat 1 tsp mustard oil in a separate pan. Add bhindi and sauté on medium heat until tender and slightly crisp. Add turmeric, red chili, coriander powder, and salt. Cook for another 5-7 minutes. Add a dash of lemon juice if desired.
For Multigrain Roti: Knead multigrain atta with water to form a soft dough. Roll into rotis and cook on a hot tawa until done.
Serve 2 Multigrain Rotis with Dal Palak and Bhindi Sabzi.

recipes.name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-fry (Indian Style)
recipes.health_benefit: Provides lean protein from chicken and a wide array of vitamins, minerals, and fiber from the diverse vegetables. Using minimal oil makes it heart-healthy.

ingredients.item: Mixed vegetables (bell peppers, broccoli, carrots, snow peas)

instructions: Marinate chicken slices with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat rice bran oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add minced garlic, julienned ginger, and green chili. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add chicken slices and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned (about 3-4 minutes). Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add sliced onions and stir-fry until softened. Add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add tomato puree, cumin powder, coriander powder, black pepper, and low-sodium soy sauce. Stir well.
Return the cooked chicken to the pan. Toss everything together for 1-2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot, optionally with a small portion of brown rice.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Salad
recipes.health_benefit: Sprouted moong dal is easily digestible and provides excellent plant-based protein and soluble fiber, which aids in managing cholesterol. It's also rich in vitamins and minerals.
instructions: Ensure moong dal is well-sprouted (can be done by soaking moong dal overnight, then draining and keeping in a muslin cloth for 1-2 days, rinsing periodically).
In a mixing bowl, combine sprouted moong dal, chopped cucumber, tomato, onion, green chili, and coriander leaves.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and black salt. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack.

recipes.name: Low-Fat Paneer and Spinach Bhurji
recipes.health_benefit: Provides lean protein from low-fat paneer and is packed with iron and vitamins from spinach. It's a satisfying and nutrient-dense breakfast option, helping to manage blood sugar.
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for 1 minute.
Add finely chopped tomato and cook until it softens and releases oil.
Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add chopped spinach and cook until it wilts completely.
Add crumbled low-fat paneer and salt. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring gently.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with whole wheat toast or multigrain roti.
